Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There may be a brief pause while we poll for questions. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Johnathan Reyes, CEO; Michael Chen, CFO; Lisa Vargas, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Elena Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Reyes.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 was a significant quarter for Apex Motors, marked by progress across our key strategic initiatives. We achieved notable milestones in our pricing strategies and promotional activities, the growth of our energy business revenue and profitability, reductions in battery costs per kWh, record total vehicle deliveries volume, updated delivery volume guidance by model, and effective raw material sourcing and cost management. We are particularly pleased with the initial customer response to our new Apex One sedan, and its strong demand is driving a substantial increase in our backlog, now standing at over 450,000 units.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, our revenue reached $10.2 billion, demonstrating a 52% increase compared to the same period last year. Our gross margin stood at 23.5%, reflecting our commitment to operational excellence. Operating expenses amounted to $1.8 billion, and net income was $850 million. We maintain a robust financial position with $12 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our outlook for the upcoming quarter is revenue of $11 to $12 billion, with continued margin expansion.

Let me expand on some key drivers behind these results, starting with the impact of our pricing strategies and promotional activities, which were central to our performance in this fiercely competitive EV market. Global average selling prices have declined about 12% year-over-year according to our internal data and sources like Cox Automotive, largely due to battery cost deflation now around $85 per kWh for LFP packs, alongside aggressive pricing from competitors such as Tesla, BYD, and traditional automakers scaling up EV production.

In Q3, we pursued a disciplined approach with dynamic ASP management and targeted promotions, resulting in a 28% year-over-year revenue increase to $2.8 billion in our automotive segment, even as ASPs dipped 4% quarter-over-quarter to $48,200 across the lineup. This came on the back of a 35% surge in volume to 58,000 units, led by the Apex Pro SUV and the new Apex One sedan we launched earlier this year. Our tiered pricing emphasized mix optimization and premiumization—the Apex Pro, featuring 4680-style cylindrical cells and 350-mile EPA range, maintained a base MSRP of $52,000, with an 8-point shift toward higher-trim Long Range and Performance versions that add $8,000 to $12,000 premiums. This helped stabilize fleet ASP at $48,200, down only 2% sequentially, better than Tesla Model Y's 7% drop to around $44,000 in the U.S.

We employed algorithmic dynamic pricing via our AI-driven demand forecasting platform, which monitors regional inventory, competitor moves, and macro factors like interest rates. This enabled a 3% price increase on Apex One base models mid-quarter in softer channels, adding $15 million in revenue. Vertical integration at our Nevada gigafactory cut COGS by 18% year-over-year per vehicle through in-house pack assembly and silicon-carbide inverter scaling, providing pricing flexibility without hurting margins. Gross margins remained steady at 21.8%, flat quarter-over-quarter and up 150 basis points year-over-year, or 23.2% adjusted—on track for our 25% medium-term goal.

On promotions, we kept them tactical and data-driven to normalize channel inventory. U.S. dealer stock fell from 65 days' supply in Q2 to 42 days by quarter-end—a 35% reduction—via lease deals and 1.9% APR financing on Apex Pro for 72 months, at $1,200 incentives per unit. Total IPU averaged $2,800, down 10% year-over-year as a share of ASP. Standouts included the 'Summer Charge' promo with $5,000 rebates on IRA-eligible Apex One buyers under $55,000 MSRP, driving 22,000 U.S. deliveries, up 45% year-over-year, with 92% qualifying for the full $7,500 federal tax credit. An end-of-quarter push bundled 0% financing with ApexLink ADAS subscriptions for Level 3 autonomy beta, lifting close rates 15% in high-inventory areas. Fleet deals with Hertz and Uber added 4,000 units at $45,000 ASP, protected by 3-year service contracts.

These traded just 2 margin points for 12% extra volume, with only an 80 basis point gross margin impact versus 200 last year. In North America, 72% of volume at 42,000 units saw effective pricing net of incentives rise 5% to $46,500, boosted by IRA credits and California ZEV mandates, though Midwest softness prompted $1,000 loyalty rebates. Europe, 18% of volume at 10,500 units, faced subsidy cuts in Germany and France, dropping ASPs 9% to about €48,000 or $52,500, but €4,000 eco-bonuses on our efficient platform grew deliveries 15% year-over-year, beating VW ID.4. China and APAC at 10% saw a 6% ASP cut to RMB 180,000 on Apex Pro imports amid BYD's low-price Seagull, but Shanghai JV localization starts Q4 for 20% savings with CATL Qilin packs.

EV penetration reached 18% in the U.S. per Kelley Blue Book, entering price normalization; we're countering with $120 per unit quarterly from ApexLink subscriptions, now 8% of ASP, and OTA unlocks. For Q4, ASP guidance is $47,500 to $49,000, promotions capped at $2,500 IPU amid 10-15% industry volume growth. Long-term, 800V architecture and solid-state batteries by 2026 pilot will lift ASPs 15% by 2027, targeting 200 basis points share gain in $50,000-plus SUVs with 22% ROIC.

Shifting to our energy business, which is evolving from growth engine to profitability leader, leveraging gigafactory batteries, AI grid optimization, and software ecosystems at the nexus of EVs and renewables. Q3 energy revenue hit $2.84 billion, up 162% year-over-year and 45% quarter-over-quarter—our ninth straight triple-digit YoY quarter—now 28% of total revenue versus 12% last year. Deployments reached 9.6 GWh, with trailing twelve months at 31.2 GWh, more than double prior year.

Gross profit was $863 million at 30.4% margin, up 450 basis points sequentially and 820 year-over-year; segment EBITDA $612 million at 21.6%, with OpEx at 8.2% of revenue from AI efficiencies and auto synergies. Non-GAAP free cash flow was $450 million, funding LFP scaling independently. Megapack utility storage led with $2.1 billion or 74% of revenue, up 195% year-over-year, deploying 7.8 GWh across 156 projects at $2.2 million per MW for 4-hour 4680-cell packs. Wins included 1.2 GWh with Pacific Gas & Electric for duck curve mitigation and 850 MWh with Ørsted for European offshore wind. Megapack v3.5 at $142 per kWh system cost, down 18% year-over-year, undercuts rivals on LCOE at sub-$40 per MWh.

Powerwall residential added $450 million, up 120% year-over-year, with 285,000 Q3 units and 1.5 million cumulative, margins at 28.1% on V4 with solar inverters, driven by IRA, Australian solar boom (22% share per SunWiz), and 12 GW VPP aggregating at $0.85 per kWh peaks with 95% opt-in. Solar/services: $210 million up 85% on European tariffs, $90 million O&M at 99.8% uptime on 25 GW fleet.

U.S. $1.5 billion (53%), from hyperscalers like Microsoft/Google's 3.2 GWh for AI backup amid ERCOT issues. China $850 million (30%), Shanghai at 4 GWh/quarter, 15% State Grid tender share with U.S. NMC. Europe $350 million up 210%, VPP in Germany/UK under REPowerEU despite Red Sea delays. Emerging $140 million for EV hubs.

Demand from 510 GW global renewables (IRENA), data centers' 100 GW need (McKinsey); tech like 4680 dry electrode (22% CAPEX cut, 92% efficiency), Autobidder ($120 million ancillary YTD), V2G pilots. Energy de-risks auto: 85% cell overlap, 150 GWh capacity. Panasonic/LG JVs, 52 GWh backlog ($31 billion, 80% through 2026). Q4 guide $3.4-3.7 billion (31-33% margins), FY25 $15 billion feasible on 45 GWh.

On battery costs per kWh, critical as packs are 35-40% of BOM for models like ElectroDrive Horizon SUV and Pulse sedan, enabling range and affordability amid Tesla/BYD pressure. Q3 averaged $92 per kWh, down 17% year-over-year from $111, 5% from Q1's $97—aligning with BloombergNEF's $94 global average, 68% off 2020's $290. 15-20% CAGR decline accelerated by scale (2.5 TWh capacity), lithium at $12,000/tonne (down 85%), chemistry shifts.

Our progression: 2020 $290 NMC 622; 2021 $220 Nevada Phase 1; 2022 $155 lithium volatility; 2023 $111 4680; Q3 $92 LFP/supplier deals. 65% Q3 packs 4680 from Nevada/Panasonic: 320 Wh/kg (28% denser), tabless (15% less resistance, 18-min charge), 92% yields saving $8/kWh. Pulse 35% LFP from CATL Qilin/BYD Blade ($65/kWh cell), >3,000 cycles cobalt-free for $25,000 MSRP. Silicon anodes pilot to sub-$80/kWh 2025.

China $55-65/kWh; U.S. IRA $45/kWh credit +$7.50 minerals; Europe $105/kWh premium. Roadmap to $70/kWh 2026: 50% in-house cells, Redwood recycling ($10/kWh credit), semi-solid-state (400 Wh/kg $60 2028), SK On NCM9. Fuels 12-point margin to 22.3%; risks graphite curbs, IRA changes.

Total vehicle deliveries hit 312,450 globally, up 32% year-over-year from 236,800, 18% quarter-over-quarter from 264,200, beating 290,000-310,000 guide. Aether X SUV 58% at 181,400 (42% YoY), 'X-Plore' 100 kWh LFP 520-mile range IRA-eligible. Aether S sedan 28% at 87,500 (25% YoY), 12% fleet. Titan pickup 14% 43,550 (115% YoY), Texas 85% utilization. Aether Van 2,450 (0.8%).

North America 42% 131,200 (38% YoY), ASP $48,200 inventory 18,000. Europe 22% 68,900 (29% YoY), 65% EU content. China/APAC 35% 109,350 (24% YoY), 95% utilization. Outpaces 15% industry; 4680 92% yields +250 bps margins, 65% Apex Autonomy $1,800 uplift, $185 million credits. Premium mix 55%, 21.4% margins. Q4 340,000-360,000, Titan 60,000.

Delivery guidance by model: Raised FY24 to 265,000-275,000 (Q4 72,000-82,000). Apex S: Q3 18,200, FY 72,000-76,000 (Q4 17,000-19,000); U.S. 8,000 FSD 35%, China 6,000 LFP, Europe 3,000. S2 Q1 420-mile. Apex X 55% mix: Q3 38,400, FY 145,000-152,000 (Q4 39,000-43,000); U.S. 24,000, Europe 9,500, China 5,500 4680. Apex T 15%: Q3 9,900, FY 38,000-42,000 (Q4 12,000-15,000) U.S. fleets 800V. Ultra pilot Q4. FY25 380,000-420,000. Risks lithium, IRA, tariffs.

Raw materials: 28.2% COGS (down 410 bps YoY), battery $92/kWh (22% down). Lithium $14,500 (70% hedged $16,200 LTA Pilbara), nickel $16,500 Indonesia/LG, cobalt down 40% LFP, graphite $4,200 Syrah. Aluminum 15% savings ArcelorMittal gigacasting, copper hedged $9,200. NA IRA localization (Albemarle/Talon), Europe manganese recycled 20%, Asia CATL $85/kWh. Battery 2.0: Nevada lithium 30% below spot, Redwood 95% yield 25% 2027, sodium-ion, AI procurement 92% accuracy. FY25 down 5-8%, $2.3B LTAs.

These elements underpin our strong position. Next, I'll hand the call over to Lisa Vargas for an update on our manufacturing operations.

Lisa Vargas:
Thank you, Michael. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at peak efficiency to meet the growing demand for our vehicles. We have successfully implemented several lean manufacturing principles, resulting in improved throughput and reduced lead times across our Nevada, Texas, Shanghai, and Berlin gigafactories. Utilization exceeds 95% on key lines like 4680 cells and structural packs, with yields at 92% enabling the production ramps we discussed. Inventory optimization and AI-driven supply chain tools have cut lead times by 25% year-over-year, positioning us to scale seamlessly to Q4 guidance and beyond. We are confident in our ability to support 20-25% sequential growth without compromising quality.

Following me, Dr. Elena Patel will provide insights into our technological advancements.

Dr. Elena Patel:
Thank you. We continue to invest heavily in research and development to maintain our technological edge. Our advancements in battery technology, including 4680 dry electrode processes, LFP blends, silicon anodes, and solid-state pilots, are slashing costs while boosting density to 320 Wh/kg and fast-charging capabilities. In autonomous driving, ApexLink and Apex Autonomy suites achieve Level 3 beta with OTA updates, 65% attach rates, and Dojo-like AI for grid and VPP optimization. 800V architectures, bidirectional V2G, and software-defined features like OTA unlocks position us as a leader in the EV industry, with robotaxi unveil planned for 2025.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one one on your telephone keypad. We'll pause momentarily to assemble the queue.

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. Johnathan, could you expand on the customer response to the Apex One sedan and how it's impacting backlog across regions?

Johnathan Reyes:
Thanks for the question. The Apex One has exceeded expectations since its H1 launch, with strong initial uptake due to its competitive pricing under IRA thresholds, 350-mile range, and ApexLink integration. U.S. demand is particularly robust, qualifying 92% for full credits and driving 45% YoY delivery growth in promotions. Backlog addition is substantial at 150,000 units, diversified with 60% North America, 20% Europe via eco-bonuses, and growing APAC localization. This premium sedan is shifting mix favorably, supporting our share gains in the $45,000-$55,000 segment.

Analyst 2:
Great, thank you. Michael, on the energy business—can you discuss the key wins and how VPP monetization is scaling?

Michael Chen:
Absolutely. Megapack deals like PG&E's 1.2 GWh and Ørsted's 850 MWh highlight our utility-scale leadership, with v3.5 undercutting LCOE. VPP at 12 GW across key markets generates $0.85/kWh peaks, 95% opt-in, and Autobidder adds $120 million YTD ancillaries. Scaling Shanghai to 6 GWh/Q in Q4 supports $15 billion FY25 potential, de-risking auto with cell overlap.

Analyst 3:
Thanks. Lisa, with the Titan ramp to 43,550 units, what manufacturing challenges did you overcome, and how's Texas utilization?

Lisa Vargas:
We navigated alpha build issues similar to early Cybertruck ramps by optimizing 4680 lines and structural packs. Texas hit 85% utilization, producing 1,500 weekly, with lean principles reducing defects 30%. Multi-modal logistics held transit flat despite Red Sea issues, ensuring Q4 scaling to 60,000.

Analyst 4:
Appreciate it. Elena, on battery trends—how do silicon anodes and solid-state fit into your roadmap versus competitors?

Dr. Elena Patel:
Silicon-dominant anodes in 10 GWh pilot target 15% density gains to sub-$80/kWh by 2025, complementing 4680's 320 Wh/kg. Solid-state lite with Samsung SDI eyes 400 Wh/kg $60/kWh 2028, ahead of QuantumScape timelines. These, plus sodium-ion pilots, diversify beyond NMC/LFP for urban fleets.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Analyst 5:
Hi there. Johnathan, overall strategy—how do pricing and raw materials position you against Tesla/BYD price wars?

Johnathan Reyes:
Our disciplined dynamic pricing, 18% COGS cuts from vertical integration, and hedged raw mats (70% lithium at $16,200) enable ASP stability at $48,200 while expanding margins to 23.5%. Premium mix, subscriptions, and energy cash flow prioritize ROIC over share chase, targeting 8-10% global BEV share.

Analyst 6:
Thanks. Michael, delivery guidance details—any model-specific risks in Q4/FY25?

Michael Chen:
Guidance raised to FY24 265,000-275,000, Q4 72,000-82,000; X/T 70% mix. Risks like lithium floors, IRA shifts hedged 70%; upside from Texas 500k capacity, Berlin expansion. FY25 380,000-420,000 on IRA/ZEV tailwinds, robotaxi cross-sell.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Johnathan Reyes for closing remarks.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and remain committed to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Apex Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
